title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: Add a calculator to the sales order page
summary: This post explains how to add a calculator control to the sales order page in Business Central using control add-in objects built with AL and JavaScript. It covers built-in calculation features, control add-in architecture, dimension properties, scripting options, and integration into pages.
key_points: Business Central natively supports inline calculations in fields using formulas like 19+19 or 12*4, but adding a dedicated calculator requires control add-in objects
Control add-ins are custom visual elements created with AL code and JavaScript that can exchange data and respond to user interactions
Control add-ins use Iframe elements and support dimension properties like RequestedHeight, MinimumWidth, MaximumHeight, and stretch/shrink behaviors
Scripts can be loaded locally from the extension or externally via HTTP(S), with separate startup, recreation, and refresh scripts available
Control add-ins are inserted into pages using the usercontrol keyword and can be embedded in factboxes or other page elements

quotes.text: A control add-in object is created with the use of AL code and JavaScript.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the core technical approach to building custom UI components beyond native AL capabilities

quotes.text: Standard Business Central already includes calculation features, but it requires you to input formulas directly into the fields.
quotes.why_it_matters: Establishes why a dedicated calculator add-in is needed despite existing calculation support

quotes.text: For each control add-in, Business Central will generate an Iframe element, where it will dynamically load the control.
quotes.why_it_matters: Clarifies the technical implementation architecture of how custom controls are rendered in the client
